It renders the SERVER-rendered template (the page's HTML is served to the sandboxed Chrome and printed). It does NOT execute the live client-side TSX/SPA. So a page whose content is computed client-side (e.g. a PAR/forecast page driven by a static/*.ts module in the browser) prints EMPTY of those computed numbers.

To PDF a client-computed report: render it as a gotmpl page fed by server-side values - compute the numbers with `run: compute` (same .ts module, server-side; see api({at:'compute'})), store/pass them, and render server-side so /pdf captures them. One algorithm, both execution paths.

The PDF holds the page and nothing the framework adds for a person at a browser: no cookie-consent banner, analytics beacon, feedback widget (features.testing / features.feedback), session recorder, live-update or reload client, web-app manifest or service worker. The app's own head.html, theme.css and layout are kept, and page script still runs; window.bmCookieConsent() answers '' there (nobody has chosen). The free plan's "Built with Benmore" attribution is printed.

Chrome's own print header and footer (date, title, address, page count) are off, for GET /pdf/<page> and for connector PDF artifacts: a sheet carries only what the page draws. For page numbers or a running header or footer, give the page CSS page margin boxes in its own <style>, e.g. `@page { margin: 20mm; @bottom-right { content: counter(page) " / " counter(pages); } }` (@top-left, @top-center, @bottom-center and the other margin boxes work the same way). Margin boxes need Chrome 131 or newer on the host.

The page is rendered as the CURRENT session - the PDF reflects what that user can see. Rendering is budgeted at 10 per minute per signed-in user, or per client address for anonymous callers (the resolved client address, an IPv6 client by its /64); past that the route answers 429 `Too many PDF requests - try again later`. Pages with auth="required" must be reachable as the caller; anonymous PDFs of authed pages don't work. The page's role, require and redirect= gates apply too: a redirect that matches the caller (including redirect="*:/" for a page taken offline) answers 303 to its target instead of a PDF. A scoped API token renders the page as its account: token scopes narrow /api/<table>, not what a page's queries select (api({at:'frontend'}) ssr_page_gates).

The renderer is sandboxed: the page is served from an isolated origin, and Chrome can load only HTTPS assets from hosts the page CSP already allows (the script CDNs the app's source names, Google Fonts, rsms.me, the media CDN, plus your app.yaml `csp:` extensions). Wildcard csp entries, plain http, loopback and private addresses, frames, forms and navigation away from the page are refused. Relative asset URLs (/static/...) do not load - use absolute https URLs on allowed hosts, or inline the CSS. To use a third-party image host, add it to `csp.img_src`.
